scope: Treatment-only gap audit of current major US veterinary oncology center listings; semantic dedup against effective catalog by center+disease+intervention+protocol/source.

upsert.title: Cryoablation or intratumoral immunotherapy before amputation for canine osteosarcoma
upsert.center: Johns Hopkins Center for Image-Guided Animal Therapy (CIGAT)
upsert.status: Open and enrolling — current Johns Hopkins CIGAT page
upsert.contacts: Johns Hopkins CIGAT — 410-502-7325; see official page for study email
upsert.funding: Study fully funds cryotherapy or investigational immunotherapy and study imaging/monitoring; required amputation and chemotherapy are owner-paid.
upsert.notes: Dogs receive either cryoablation or two doses of tumor-injected investigational immunotherapy before required amputation, followed by chemotherapy.

upsert.title: Radiation therapy plus oral chemotherapy for canine brain tumors
upsert.center: Johns Hopkins Center for Image-Guided Animal Therapy (CIGAT)
upsert.status: Open and enrolling — current Johns Hopkins CIGAT page
upsert.contacts: Johns Hopkins CIGAT — 410-502-7325; see official page for study email
upsert.funding: Radiation therapy, chemotherapy, prescribed supportive medications, follow-up MRI and blood tests are fully funded by the study; treatment for progression is not covered.
upsert.notes: Five consecutive workdays of radiation with concurrent oral TMZ for an intra-axial suspected glioma restricted to one side of the brain.

upsert.title: Kubanda cryotherapy for canine mammary cancer
upsert.center: Johns Hopkins Center for Image-Guided Animal Therapy (CIGAT) / Kubanda Cryotherapy
upsert.status: Recruiting — Phase IB trial listed on current Johns Hopkins CIGAT page
upsert.contacts: Contact Kubanda Cryotherapy through the email listed on the official Johns Hopkins trial page
upsert.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with the study team.
upsert.notes: Phase IB veterinary cryotherapy-device treatment trial for dogs with mammary cancer.

upsert.title: IF7-SN38 chemotherapy for canine metastatic cancer
upsert.center: Johns Hopkins Veterinary Clinical Trials Network
upsert.status: Listed on current Johns Hopkins VCTN clinical-trials page
upsert.contacts: Johns Hopkins Veterinary Clinical Trials Network — 410-614-0105; see official page for email
upsert.funding: Confirm current study-covered and owner-paid costs with VCTN.
upsert.notes: Novel IF7-SN38 chemotherapy delivered intravenously every other day for three to five days; planned enrollment 5–10 dogs.

upsert.title: Hypofractionated radiation plus gilvetmab for canine oligometastatic lung cancer
upsert.center: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
upsert.status: Funded treatment study — current 2026 University of Illinois trial announcement
upsert.contacts: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital — 217-265-6554; see current oncology trial listing
upsert.funding: Funded study; confirm exact owner-paid and study-covered costs with Illinois.
upsert.notes: All enrolled dogs receive hypofractionated radiation to 1–5 pulmonary metastatic lesions plus anti-PD-1 canine monoclonal antibody gilvetmab; randomized only between two radiation schedules, not treatment versus placebo.

upsert.title: Local T-cell engager hydrogel immunotherapy before surgery for canine soft tissue sarcoma
upsert.center: Washington State University Veterinary Teaching Hospital
upsert.status: Recruiting — current WSU clinical study page
upsert.contacts: Jennifer Heusser, Clinical Studies Coordinator — 509-592-3668; jpmarcus3@wsu.edu
upsert.funding: Study contributes $1,000 toward the medical bill and covers ICU stay, study-related medications and study bloodwork; owners pay standard-of-care surgery/diagnostics.
upsert.notes: Dose-escalation local anticancer immunotherapy: hydrogel plus T-cell engager is injected into the tumor seven days before standard surgical removal. WSU notes direct therapeutic benefit is not guaranteed.
